slides.heading: Community Health Nursing
slides.subtitle: Nursing + public health to promote health and prevent illness in population groups — delivered outside the hospital.

slides.heading: What CHN Is
bullets: A synthesis of nursing knowledge/practice with the science and practice of public health.
Applied through the nursing process to promote health and prevent illness in population groups.
Care is comprehensive, general, continual — NOT episodic.
Recognizes the population as a whole and the impact of many factors on health.
Nurse and client have greater control and collaborate as equals in health decisions.

slides.heading: Focus: Health Promotion & Illness Prevention
bullets: Health promotion — raise the level of health through a healthy lifestyle (nutrition, diet, exercise, rest, stop smoking).
Illness prevention — specific protection (e.g., immunization, health teaching).
Ideal Body Weight (IBW): <10 yrs use growth chart; >10 yrs use BMI.

slides.heading: Goal
bullets: Optimum level of functioning — the highest level of wellness for the population.

terms.definition: Health assessment once a year; safety of students.
Company nurse — health and safety of employees (50+ employees requires a company nurse).
Mental hygiene; addresses community mental-health issues. Governed by the Mental Health Law (RA 11036) — the first mental health act.
Stigma (mark of shame) and violation of human rights.

slides.heading: Key Takeaways
bullets: CHN = nursing + public health, delivered to populations outside the hospital.
Core aims: promote health, prevent illness; goal = optimum level of functioning.
Subspecialties: school, occupational, and mental health nursing.
Mental Health Law = RA 11036 (first mental health act).
